segments.source: What must be true about the order of New school and Founding? Can the exact order of Flood and Bridge opening be determined?

1. From New school before Bridge opening and Bridge opening before Founding, infer New school before Founding. 2. Flood is only constrained to be after New school. There is no stated relation between Flood and Bridge opening. 3. Therefore the first comparison is forced but the second is underdetermined.
New school must be before Founding. The relative order of Flood and Bridge opening cannot be determined from the given facts.
A careful reasoner distinguishes what must be true from what merely could be true.

Problem 804. Ordering the events of Lake District
Historical chronology often starts from partial information: some events are ordered relative to others even when exact dates are not known.
Flood happened before Founding. Founding happened before Bridge opening. New school happened after Flood. Market charter happened after Bridge opening.
“Before” is transitive: if A is before B and B is before C, then A is before C. If two events are not connected by the facts, their relative order may be undetermined.

Dates can be used as numbers, but historical labels such as centuries follow explicit conventions.
An institution was founded in 1699 and reorganized in 1731. Use the rule: years 1–100 are the 1st century, 101–200 the 2nd, and so on. Duration is end year minus start year.
Apply the century rule mechanically; do not infer a century from the first two digits alone. Compute elapsed time by subtraction.
How many years passed between the two events? In which centuries did 1699 and 1731 fall?
32 years; 1699 is in the 17th century and 1731 in the 18th century.
